prompt: An independent retry model has a fixed positive success probability. If that probability halves while remaining positive, what happens to the expected total attempts through success?

options.text: It becomes infinite for any probability below one.
options.explanation: The failure tail decays geometrically when success probability is positive.

options.text: It doubles, although individual waits still vary.
options.explanation: The geometric mean is the reciprocal of success probability.

options.text: It halves because success is rarer.
options.explanation: Rarer success requires more attempts on average.

options.text: It becomes a hard maximum number of attempts.
options.explanation: Expectation does not bound every possible wait.

workedExample: Each failure restarts the same waiting process under the model. Reducing the success chance increases average retry load. Keep that model conclusion separate from real overload, where attempts can be dependent and alter the success chance.
